title: Consolidate Pods: one model, less code, a simpler database
summary: Pods carries two orchestration models, two mobile channels, six decision sources and 158 tables from earlier experiments. This plan removes the unused paths, keeps networks as the only model, gives MCP full access through the owner's DDISA login and leaves every approval at the IdP.

problem.statement: The same information exists in several diverging forms: workflows and networks, two chat models, two inbox channels, five configuration stores.
problem.impact: Every change needs several producers, templates and guards, and safety rules built for abandoned paths block real work.
problem.approach: Delete dead code, migrate live workflows to networks, collapse decisions and storage, and replace MCP access modes with an owner login.
problem.outcome: One network model, one decision path, one baseline schema, and an MCP that can do everything except approve grants.

goal: Reduce Pods to the model that is actually used, without interrupting the live Delta Mind mail network and the active monitors.
context: Audit of main ca1e917d on October 9, 2026: 158 desktop tables over 41 migration steps, 25 relay tables in three databases, about 70 network tables beside 22 workflow/graph tables, three mail pipelines, decisions from six sources, about 1.6k LOC of unmounted UI and about 700 unused i18n keys. Pods has no prompt-injection detector or taint tracking, but several structural rules encode that reasoning. Live state: one active network (Delta Mind mail, 750 done), one active workflow (Morgenbriefing · Mail-Prüfung) and three paused workflows (IURIO DOCPIT, Linde portal, Linde server report). Tracking issue: https://repos.openape.ai/patrick/monorepo/issues/1455.
scope: apps/openape-pods (desktop, worker, renderer, MCP), apps/openape-pods-relay, packages/pods-protocol.
Removal of apps/openape-pods-ios and the encrypted pods-mobile channel.
Migration of the live workflows: convert Morgenbriefing, archive the three paused ones.
MCP authentication through the owner's DDISA account and the move of desktop self-approvals to the IdP.
nonGoals: No new product features and no UI redesign beyond removing dead paths.
No change to IdP grant semantics; Pods never approves a grant.
packages/prompt-injection-detector, troop and ape-agent stay untouched.
No restore support for backups older than schema 41.

milestones.title: Sandbox and grants on network and Pod level
milestones.goal: The sandbox decides what a Pod can execute, the grant what it may do; the owner identity grants at setup and at runtime, also through the Codex owner session.
steps: Prototype done: the IdP already lets the owner identity approve, deny and revoke with an apes-cli owner token, and grant details can cover whole programs and HTTP origins with methods. No specification change: approvals through the MCP owner session are the owner's own decisions, like a logged-in CLI; reusable access means the owner approves each brokered request as always, not IdP standing-grant policies.

Sandbox as its own concept on network and Pod level: whole programs, HTTP origins with methods, directories, secrets and the OS sandbox level up to running as the owner's macOS user (paths and reach only); network members inherit the network sandbox; no read/write authorization split. The DDISA identity is always the Pod.

Grants independent of the sandbox: always requested by the Pod identity (a network-level grant declaration is issued to each member Pod) and decided by the owner identity at the IdP page, on the desktop, or by Codex during the one-hour owner session, which keeps the owner token in memory only; after expiry nothing is approved automatically.
Adapter read/write metadata decides only whether a failed run is replayed automatically; grants made through Codex are marked and visible in the decisions.
acceptance: Codex with an owner session can create the Morgenbriefing network with its sandbox and grants without a human click; after the session expires, a new grant request waits for the owner.
Without a grant nothing executes even if the sandbox allows it; without the sandbox nothing executes even if a grant exists.

milestones.title: MCP sign-in confirmed on the phone
milestones.goal: The owner confirms the one-hour MCP session from the phone; a remote Codex tells him how, and nobody needs to sit at the Mac.
steps: Without a session, Pods opens an IdP QR channel (existing /api/session/qr flow) and returns the confirmation link in the login_required tool error and as an inbox entry.

After the phone confirmation, Pods claims the session, mints the owner token through the existing PKCE authorization and binds the one-hour session to the shim connection; the Mac confirmation dialog is removed.

Alternatively the owner's logged-in apes CLI (human, owner email, issuer id.openape.ai) proves the owner session without phone or Mac; sessions renew while apes stays logged in, and apes logout ends them.

The MCP tells the tool user to keep checking the sign-in state: login_required carries the link and the instruction to poll a session status action every few seconds until signed in (or expired), then continue; Codex therefore knows when it may use MCP again.
The IdP confirmation page explains remote confirmation and shows the requesting device; the owner confirms only links from his Pods inbox or Codex session.
acceptance: A remote Codex session gets the link, the owner confirms on the phone, and the next tool call succeeds without any action at the Mac.
An unconfirmed, denied or expired channel leaves no session.

sections.title: Audit findings in numbers
sections.body:
- Desktop: 158 tables, 41 migration steps, about 65k LOC.
- Relay: 25 tables in three databases, two operations tables, two device registries.
- Duplicates: workflows vs networks, two chat models, binding revision stored three times, five configuration stores, decisions from six sources, snapshot as rows and views.
- Dead code: about 1.6k LOC unmounted UI, about 700 unused i18n keys, unused commands and dependencies.
- Self-approvals today: main/programs/grants.ts and connections/runtime-grant.ts approve with the owner bearer.

sections.title: Safety mechanisms that stay
sections.body: IdP grants for CLI and HTTP commands and HTTPS destinations, owner-decided grants for mail moves, the effect ledger with idempotency keys, hash-bound executables, secret isolation and redaction, and the owner identity check at run start.

handoff: Plan complete. Follow-ups outside this plan: Pod-identity SP exchange for issue reads in the Morgenbriefing; phone sign-in with IdP-verified initiator; Mail-Prüfung time budget per account; IURIO PR monitor interrupted run; WAL checkpoint after upgrade; IdP client_id metadata check; IdP refresh act/delegation; Jev probability tolerance.

changelog.text: Revision 1 drafted from the audit of main ca1e917d and the owner's four decisions.
Owner approved revision 1 with "Go"; M1 merged as b757dafc; M2 and M3 started.
Revision 2: M3 found that Morgenbriefing is a sequence workflow and MCP cannot create networks, so M7 moves before M3 and the paused workflows are archived by the M4 migration.
Owner confirmed revision 2 and chose the Pods-driven MCP login; M2 merged as 26532557.
M6 narrowed: the archive-behind-approve-gate rule stays because the gate is the owner approval (issue 1454); M6 split into part A (parallel to M7) and part B (after M7).

M7 merged as PR 329 and PR 330; M6 part A merged as PR 331 after five security findings were fixed with refusal tests. A Morgenbriefing network needs fresh Pods and a ported script API, and a join only merges inputs of the same source item.
M6 part B merged as PR 332 (approvals only at the IdP, in-app master turn removed) and M5 as PR 333 (route-only networks, schema 42); gate once/always moved from M6 to M5.

Revision 3: the Morgenbriefing preparation showed that consumers may not read programs and networks have no HTTP or secrets; the owner chose to relax these rules (M6 part C) instead of a workaround. The M4 branch is ready and waits for M3.

M6 part C merged as PR 334. Revision 4: the owner separated sandbox (can) from grant (may) on network and Pod level and allowed the Codex owner session to grant single and standing grants as the owner; this supersedes the earlier rule that MCP never approves. The prepared Morgenbriefing needed 16 approvals under the old model.

M6d prototype: owner-token approvals work with the existing IdP; the owner rejected a DDISA profile change because MCP is his tool used under his identity, so reusable access uses always approvals of brokered requests.
Revision 5: M7c lets the owner confirm the MCP sign-in on the phone through the IdP QR channel; the owner gave a proactive go for the relay, IdP and desktop rollouts.
Owner accepted the logged-in apes CLI as MCP owner-session proof and grant approver ("Ja das passt. Ich will dass du das nun so autark durchziehst"); notification delay merged as PR 335.

Four desktop releases (f5e1ee53, 2de87e10, 22eed69d, 8b336ea9) with paired backups; the first lost stored grants (bridged by owner approvals through apes, fixed by PR 340). Owner chose full reach for the owner level with a configurable denylist (PR 341). M3 completed live: Morgenbriefing network delivered Telegram message 249.
M4 (PR 344), M9 docs (PR 345) and M8 (PR 346, 347) merged and installed; acceptance Test Run published; plan closed as achieved.

entries.source: Sandbox and grants on network and Pod level
entries.text: Sandbox und Grants auf Network- und Pod-Ebene

entries.source: The sandbox decides what a Pod can execute, the grant what it may do; the owner identity grants at setup and at runtime, also through the Codex owner session.
entries.text: Die Sandbox entscheidet, was ein Pod ausführen kann, der Grant, was er darf; die Owner-Identität erteilt Grants beim Setup und zur Laufzeit, auch über die Codex-Owner-Session.

entries.source: Prototype done: the IdP already lets the owner identity approve, deny and revoke with an apes-cli owner token, and grant details can cover whole programs and HTTP origins with methods. No specification change: approvals through the MCP owner session are the owner's own decisions, like a logged-in CLI; reusable access means the owner approves each brokered request as always, not IdP standing-grant policies.
entries.text: Prototyp erledigt: Der IdP erlaubt der Owner-Identität bereits Freigeben, Ablehnen und Widerrufen mit einem apes-cli-Owner-Token, und Grant-Details können ganze Programme und HTTP-Origins mit Methoden abdecken. Keine Spec-Änderung: Freigaben über die MCP-Owner-Session sind Entscheidungen des Owners selbst, wie mit einem eingeloggten CLI; wiederverwendbarer Zugriff heißt, dass der Owner jede Broker-Anfrage als always freigibt, nicht IdP-Standing-Grant-Policies.

entries.source: Sandbox as its own concept on network and Pod level: whole programs, HTTP origins with methods, directories, secrets and the OS sandbox level up to running as the owner's macOS user (paths and reach only); network members inherit the network sandbox; no read/write authorization split. The DDISA identity is always the Pod.
entries.text: Sandbox als eigenes Konzept auf Network- und Pod-Ebene: ganze Programme, HTTP-Origins mit Methoden, Ordner, Secrets und die OS-Sandbox-Stufe bis zur Ausführung als macOS-Benutzer des Owners (nur Pfade und Reichweite); Network-Mitglieder erben die Network-Sandbox; keine Trennung von Lesen und Schreiben bei der Berechtigung. Die DDISA-Identität ist immer der Pod.

entries.source: Grants independent of the sandbox: always requested by the Pod identity (a network-level grant declaration is issued to each member Pod) and decided by the owner identity at the IdP page, on the desktop, or by Codex during the one-hour owner session, which keeps the owner token in memory only; after expiry nothing is approved automatically.
entries.text: Grants unabhängig von der Sandbox: immer von der Pod-Identität angefragt (eine Grant-Deklaration auf Network-Ebene wird für jedes Mitglied ausgestellt) und entschieden von der Owner-Identität auf der IdP-Seite, am Desktop oder durch Codex während der einstündigen Owner-Session, die das Owner-Token nur im Speicher hält; nach Ablauf wird nichts automatisch freigegeben.

entries.source: Adapter read/write metadata decides only whether a failed run is replayed automatically; grants made through Codex are marked and visible in the decisions.
entries.text: Die Lese/Schreib-Metadaten des Adapters entscheiden nur noch, ob ein fehlgeschlagener Lauf automatisch wiederholt wird; über Codex erteilte Grants sind markiert und in den Entscheidungen sichtbar.

entries.source: Without a grant nothing executes even if the sandbox allows it; without the sandbox nothing executes even if a grant exists.
entries.text: Ohne Grant wird nichts ausgeführt, auch wenn die Sandbox es erlaubt; ohne Sandbox wird nichts ausgeführt, auch wenn ein Grant existiert.

entries.source: Audit findings in numbers
entries.text: Befunde in Zahlen

entries.source:
- Desktop: 158 tables, 41 migration steps, about 65k LOC.
- Relay: 25 tables in three databases, two operations tables, two device registries.
- Duplicates: workflows vs networks, two chat models, binding revision stored three times, five configuration stores, decisions from six sources, snapshot as rows and views.
- Dead code: about 1.6k LOC unmounted UI, about 700 unused i18n keys, unused commands and dependencies.
- Self-approvals today: main/programs/grants.ts and connections/runtime-grant.ts approve with the owner bearer.
entries.text:
- Desktop: 158 Tabellen, 41 Migrationsschritte, rund 65k LOC.
- Relay: 25 Tabellen in drei Datenbanken, zwei Operations-Tabellen, zwei Gerätelisten.
- Doppelungen: Workflows und Networks, zwei Chat-Modelle, Binding-Revision dreifach, fünf Konfigurationsspeicher, Entscheidungen aus sechs Quellen, Snapshot als Zeilen und Views.
- Toter Code: rund 1,6k LOC nicht eingebundene UI, rund 700 ungenutzte i18n-Keys, ungenutzte Befehle und Abhängigkeiten.
- Selbstfreigaben heute: main/programs/grants.ts und connections/runtime-grant.ts geben mit dem Owner-Bearer frei.

The prepared Morgenbriefing needed 16 approvals under the old model.

Das vorbereitete Morgenbriefing hätte im alten Modell 16 Freigaben gebraucht.
